Part 1: Key decisions and facts

Go/no-go gates. NO at an early gate costs the least.

# Question Threshold Evidence If NO
1 Are all three contraflow exits live with interoperable Guard/agency radio nets by T+1 h? Contraflow active on West, North and East exits by T+1 h; two-way nets confirmed at all three gates; at least 4 Guard signal teams on hand; gate load within 10% of the 50/30/20 split. Control-point reports and interoperability check at T+1 h; hourly vehicle counts from T+1 h. Delay contraflow release and run staged departures by printed route card (premortem FM6 stop rule); divert the overflow to the nearest surviving exit. Gate G1 timing is then at risk and must be re-planned at T+2 h.
2 Do the UC have a published USGS trigger matrix and verbal authorization from the MT, WY and ID governors for Zone One and Scenario Beta orders? USGS final indicator values (placeholder: modeled VEI-7 probability of 20% or more in the remaining window) published by T+3 h; verbal authorization from all three governors by T+6 h; FEMA Region 10 liaison seated at T+0. USGS trigger-matrix release at T+3 h; governor confirmation calls logged by T+6 h; liaison seated at the Denver RRCC at T+0. Scenario Beta and Zone One orders cannot be called pre-authorized. Use a staged decision cell, with each governor issuing orders individually, and record the loss of the 30-minute order time. Do not start Zone One expansion on a single state's authority without a UC decision.
3 Is Gate G1 met at T+6 h? At least 98% of 35,800 (about 35,084) confirmed out by exit counts; no more than about 716 (incl. backcountry) under active sweep; responder coverage at least 50% at every post (at least 67 concurrent positions confirmed). Exit counts reconciled against lodging manifests and permits at the T+5 h checkpoint and at T+6 h; staffed-position count; backcountry sweep status. Treat G1 as slipped. Seat the standby reserve and request out-of-region Guard, apply the loss-of-exit rule (exit not restorable within 6 h: shelter in place and redirect), and hold the Zone One phase start until a sweep plan is set. Nothing downstream is downsized, but Zone One timing is re-planned.
4 Is an interim ranked hub list of at least 5 hubs outside the 500 km ring issued with written capacity confirmation by T+12 h? At least 5 hubs verified outside 500 km (Denver and Cheyenne are the only qualifying hubs named so far; distances not verified) with written capacity. The documents give 50,000 and 250,000 beds as the minimum; 250,000 is the more defensible floor, and the millions in the ring are not covered. Desktop distance and ash-exposure check and capacity statements from host emergency managers, reported at T+12 h. Hold the outer rings (100-250 km and 250-500 km) in later time bands and publish only the verified list. Run Beta as a staged decision cell instead of automatic authority, and add only hubs verified outside the ring.
5 Is Gate G2 met at T+24 h with shelters safe and supplied? At least 95% of registered Zone One residents out; perimeter staffed; interim destination list issued; shelters sited for at least 35,800 (15,000 Bozeman, 10,000 Idaho Falls, 10,800 third site); water at shelters by T+24 h (realistic T+18-30 h); PM10 below 100 ug/m3, or a relocation order within 4 h of exceedance. Zone One census and exit counts (census by T+6 h); shelter occupancy dashboard; convoy arrival times; hourly PM10 sensor feeds. Halt new intake at the affected shelter and divert arrivals; move to ranked 50+ km upwind backups (must accept 10,000 within 8 h); draw on the USD 5-10 million relocation reserve only; release the forward-depot water and the 100,000 N95 reserve.
6 By Month 2, are signed host MOUs from at least 5 hubs outside the 500 km ring and a written cost-share for shelters and hubs in place? At least 5 hubs with signed MOUs by Month 2; written federal vs state/local/host cost-share by Month 1 (fewer than 3 states signed by Month 1 is the FM7 tripwire); governor MOUs and EMAC signed by Month 1; full multi-state exercise by Month 3. Signed MOUs and cost-share letters (Month 1 and Month 2); exercise results (Month 3). Suspend automatic 500 km authority and revert to a staged decision cell (premortem FM2/FM7 stop rules). Keep the Zone Zero and Zone One response at its current scope, and scale back the Beta pre-positioning of USD 20-40 million until funding is settled.

The plan can safely run the Zone Zero evacuation, contraflow, communications and aviation grounding meanwhile. 1. Scenario Beta before MOUs are signed (🔴 High)

Decision: If the Beta trigger fires inside the 72 h window before hubs and MOUs exist, does the UC issue the 500 km order in rings on the interim list, or hold in a staged decision cell?

Why it is open: Executive Summary, Review 2.1 and Pitch call Beta pre-authorized and executable; the hub list is due T+12 h, MOUs Month 2 (2026-12-14), exercise Month 3 (2027-01-14). No document says what happens before then.

Option Consequences What changes in the plan
A. Issue the 500 km order in rings on the interim list only (0-100 km first, outer rings later). Keeps the 30-minute order time; outer rings depend on unverified hubs and may lack capacity. scenario_beta_trigger, scenario_beta_execution_rings; relabel Month 2 (2026-12-14) gate as hardening.
B. Hold in a staged decision cell until hubs are verified. Loses the 30-minute order time and risks uncontrolled shadow evacuation; safer on destination capacity. scenario_beta_trigger, governance matrix, Executive Summary, Pitch.
C. Order only 0-100 km immediately; release outer rings once at least 5 hubs are confirmed. Hybrid; delays the outer rings by hours. scenario_beta_execution_rings, scenario_beta_plan_milestones.
  • If nobody decides: The plan keeps the 'pre-authorized' claim with no valid basis; the UC improvises when the trigger fires.
  • Owner: Unified Command Strategic Oversight Board with FEMA Region VIII, on the governors' advice
  • Decide by: Month 0 (2026-10-14), before T+3 h: the trigger can fire inside the 72 h window and the matrix is published at T+3 h.
  • Blocks: Scenario Beta order; T+12 h interim hub list; Month 2 (2026-12-14) no-go gate.

Why it is open: The pitch and reviews say pre-authorized; canonical governor_authorization is only verbal by T+6 h and USGS values exist only at T+3 h.

  • If nobody decides: No one holds clear authority T+0 to T+6 h; Zone One start waits on calls, risking delay at the G1 peak.
  • Owner: Unified Command with the MT, WY and ID governors
  • Decide by: Month 0 (2026-10-14), before T+0: needed during the peak evacuation.
  • Blocks: Zone One expansion start (T+6 h); Scenario Beta orders; Gate G1.

3. Hub capacity floor and qualifying hubs (🔴 High)

Decision: What single capacity floor and which hubs outside the 500 km ring will be used for Beta?

Why it is open: A1 uses 50,000 beds; FM2 and Self-Audit use 250,000; the ring holds millions. Only Denver and Cheyenne qualify; Review 12.3 uses Utah/Idaho, which are inside the ring.

Option Consequences What changes in the plan
A. Floor 250,000 beds across at least 5 verified hubs outside 500 km. More defensible; needs 3+ more named hubs after a distance check; still below the ring population. Premortem A1/FM2, Self-Audit 11, Review 12.3, scenario_beta_second_stage_hubs.
B. Keep 50,000 beds as the minimum. Easier to meet at T+12 h; far under-sized for the ring. Premortem FM2, Self-Audit.
C. Size the floor to a stated share of the ring population once estimated. Most rigorous; needs a population figure (not quantified); delays the number. scenario_beta_population, hub thresholds.
  • If nobody decides: Conflicting thresholds persist; the T+12 h list of 5 hubs may fail by design.
  • Owner: FEMA Region VIII Regional Administrator with the UC
  • Decide by: Month 0 (2026-10-14), before T+12 h interim hub list.
  • Blocks: T+12 h interim hub list; Month 1 (2026-11-14) written plan; Month 2 (2026-12-14) MOUs.

4. Financing of shelters, hubs and state costs (🟡 Medium)

Decision: What is the federal vs state/local/host split for shelter sites, secondary hubs and state costs, and what counts against the USD 200 million envelope?

Why it is open: Canonical says OPEN. Reviews 11/Self-Audit 6 date it Month 0 (2026-10-14) and T+12 h, others Month 1 or 2 (2026-11-14, 2026-12-14); Self-Audit 18 shows a 10-20% state match as if settled.

Option Consequences What changes in the plan
A. Federal funds 100% of pre-positioning. Fast MOU signing; raises federal draw within the USD 160 million base. financing_open_decision, readiness_package_cost, FM7.
B. Federal plus state match (e.g. 10-20%). Lowers federal cost; slows MOUs and risks the FM7 tripwire (fewer than 3 states by Month 1 = 2026-11-14). financing_open_decision, Self-Audit 18, governor MOUs.
C. Host-community in-kind contribution. Least federal cost; hubs may decline, reducing capacity. financing_open_decision, hub MOUs.
  • If nobody decides: MOUs stall; Beta pre-positioning (USD 20-40 million) scaled back; FM7 stop rule triggers.
  • Owner: FEMA Region VIII finance lead with the governors
  • Decide by: Month 1 (2026-11-14): the signed-MOU milestone.
  • Blocks: Governor MOUs and EMAC (Month 1 = 2026-11-14); host MOUs (Month 2 = 2026-12-14); Beta pre-positioning.

5. Zone One shelter demand (🟡 Medium)

Decision: Are Zone One residents inside the 35,800 shelter capacity or additional, and what overflow or self-supply approach applies?

Why it is open: Shelters and water are sized for Zone Zero only; Gate G2 needs 95% of Zone One out, and the base is not quantified (census due T+6 h).

Option Consequences What changes in the plan
A. Count Zone One within 35,800 using a county/lodging proxy at T+0-T+3 h. No added capacity; likely overrun. shelter_capacity_plan, zone_one_resident_population.
B. Add overflow capacity beyond 35,800. Raises cost and water/N95 needs; the site list needs a larger ranking. shelter_capacity_plan, water_supply_target, budget.
C. Outer-zone self-supply message with limited shelter. Lower cost; relies on residents' own means. communications_stack, phase2_go_gate.
  • If nobody decides: Zone One residents have no planned shelter; G2 cannot be assessed.
  • Owner: Unified Command, Shelter Siting & Air-Quality Assurance Panel
  • Decide by: Month 0 (2026-10-14), T+6 h: shelter sites are chosen then.
  • Blocks: Gate G2 at T+24 h; shelter siting at T+6 h.

Focus and Context

A 72-hour multi-state evacuation plan for Yellowstone National Park evacuates 35,800 people (Zone Zero: T+0 to T+6h) and regional communities (Zone One: T+6 to T+24h), with pre-authorized Scenario Beta expansion to 500 km if USGS eruption indicators trigger. The plan hardens operational readiness through signed MOUs, supply pre-positioning, and full-scale exercises by Month 3 (2027-01-14), establishing the first Yellowstone-scale evacuation framework under extreme time pressure and volcanic ashfall hazard.

Purpose and Goals

Primary goals: (1) Clear 35,800 Zone Zero evacuees via three contraflow exits by T+6h (Gate G1: ≥98% confirmation); (2) evacuate 100 km Zone One residents by T+24h (Gate G2: ≥95%); (3) finalize and pre-authorize Scenario Beta second-stage hub plan with signed MOUs by Month 2 (2026-12-14) to enable 500 km expansion if triggered. Success criteria: zero authority gaps at state boundaries, real-time shelter siting under ashfall monitoring, and responder relief depth sustained through T+72h.

Key Deliverables and Outcomes

• Zone Zero clearance certified by T+6h via exit counts and backcountry sweep status. • Zone One evacuation ≥95% by T+24h with perimeter security active. • Interim ranked hub list (≥5 hubs outside 500 km ring) published by T+12h; written Scenario Beta plan by Month 1 (2026-11-14); signed host MOUs by Month 2 (2026-12-14). • Water/N95/fuel convoys dispatched by T+12h; target arrival at shelters T+24h via forward depots (realistic T+18–30h, estimate); success criterion is forward-depot pre-staging of 200,000–300,000 L (estimate). • Full-scale exercises (Beta routing, shift rotation, shelters) completed by Month 3 (2027-01-14). • After-action report and institutional-memory documentation finalized by Month 3 (2027-01-14).

Timeline and Budget

Operational response: Month 0 (2026-10-14) T+0 to T+72h. Hardening: Months 1–3 (2026-11-14 to 2027-01-14). Budget: USD 200 million envelope (range USD 150–250 million estimate); USD 47.5–87 million readiness package; USD 30–35 million free contingency after shelter relocation reserve. Pre-event capital (sensors, exercises, MOUs) funded from base; Scenario Beta hub pre-positioning within envelope.

Risks and Mitigations

Risk 1 (Critical): Scenario Beta has no executable second-stage destinations, risking cascade failure of Zone Zero evacuation. Mitigation: Finalize written plan with 5–10 named hubs (outside 500 km) and signed MOUs by Month 2 (2026-12-14); issue interim hub list by T+12h. Risk 2 (Critical): Responder staffing (100–150 rangers) has zero relief depth; single incident halts a corridor 2–4h. Mitigation: Pre-authorize 30–50 standby reserve deployable within 4 h of T+0 and Guard reinforcement if coverage <50%. Risk 3 (Critical): Shelter siting at T+6h with ±50 km forecast uncertainty and no real-time monitoring places 10,000–15,000 evacuees in heavy ashfall. Mitigation: Deploy PM10 sensors by T+0, pre-authorize 4-hour relocation protocols with backup sites 50+ km upwind.

Audience Tailoring

Audience: FEMA Regions VIII and X, state governors (Montana, Wyoming, Idaho), NPS incident management, hospital and utility executives, and multi-state Unified Command stakeholders. Tone: operational, directive, risk-transparent. Detail emphasizes life-safety milestones (Gates G1, G2), blocking dependencies (Scenario Beta hub MOUs), and resource readiness metrics rather than theoretical frameworks.

Action Orientation

By T+0 (Month 0 = 2026-10-14): Seat Unified Command and Region 10 liaison, deploy Guard signal teams and PM10 sensors, position tow/rockfall teams. By T+1h: Contraflow active on all three exits. By T+6h: Obtain verbal governor authorization; census of Zone One residents; assess Gate G1 (≥98% of 35,800 out). By T+12h: Issue Scenario Beta interim hub list; dispatch water/fuel convoys. By T+24h: Confirm Gate G2 (≥95% Zone One cleared); water/N95 arrival targeted via forward depots (realistic T+18–30h, estimate). By Month 1 (2026-11-14): Sign governor MOUs and EMAC agreements, finalize Scenario Beta written plan. By Month 2 (2026-12-14): Secure signed host MOUs from 5–10 hubs outside 500 km ring. By Month 3 (2027-01-14): Complete full-scale Beta, shift-rotation, and water-convoy exercises; publish after-action report.

Overall Takeaway

This plan transforms Yellowstone volcanic evacuation from theoretical risk to operational readiness: 35,800 people move in 6 hours via pre-authorized corridors and unified command; regional life-support (shelter, water, power, respirators) is hardened through signed interstate MOUs and supply pre-positioning; and a 500 km Scenario Beta expansion is executable—not hollow—only if second-stage hubs are named, validated and committed by Month 2 (2026-12-14). Without these three blocking dependencies (Scenario Beta plan, responder relief depth, ashfall monitoring), residual cascade-failure risk remains unacceptable. With them, the plan delivers life-safety assurance delivered by a USD 47.5–87 million readiness package (estimate) within the USD 200 million planning envelope and sets the institutional precedent for Yellowstone readiness in the 40-year eruption window.

Feedback

Strengthen by adding: (1) Explicit cost-benefit analysis (USD 47.5–87 million readiness package (estimate) vs. USD 500–800M post-event emergency response + 20–50 preventable deaths averted; USD 200 million is the planning envelope). (2) Quantified Zone One resident population from census by T+6h (population currently unquantified). (3) Distance verification (Denver, Cheyenne to Yellowstone) confirming they lie outside 500 km ring. (4) Financing clarity: federal vs. state/local/host-community cost-share for shelters and secondary hubs by Month 1 (2026-11-14). (5) Responder staffing validation: confirm actual Ranger headcount and pre-authorize Guard reinforcement commitment in signed letters by Month 1 (2026-11-14). (6) Water-convoy realistic arrival time (T+18–30h, not T+12h dispatch) and forward-depot pre-staging (200,000–300,000 liters, estimate) to close the 18–24h shelter water-supply gap if convoys are delayed.

Part 2: Supporting analysis

Persuasive elevator pitch.

Yellowstone Volcanic Evacuation Readiness Plan

Project Overview

When a volcano wakes, 35,800 people must move in six hours. Yellowstone sits above one of Earth's most volatile caldera systems. A VEI-6 eruption has a 40% probability within the next 72 hours. This project hardens the evacuation of Zone Zero (the park) and a 100 km ring of gateway towns, ensuring that when the alarm sounds, three contraflow corridors, a unified command chain, and pre-positioned shelter and supply networks activate within minutes—not days. Without it, gridlock, communication failure, or ash-stranded responders cascade into a multi-state catastrophe. With it, 35,800 people walk away, and regional hospitals and utilities stay online under ashfall. This is operational readiness at scale.

The plan moves from immediate evacuation (Phases 1 and 2, T+0 to T+24 hours) to pre-authorized escalation (Scenario Beta, 500 km ring) if eruption probability rises. All actions at T+0 onward proceed under verbal governor authorization by T+6 hours, with MOUs by Month 1 (2026-11-14); pre-event hardening occurs in Months 1–3 (2026-11-14 to 2027-01-14), with signed interstate Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs), validated shelter hubs, and full-scale exercises cementing the framework before any eruption occurs.

Target Audience

  • FEMA Regional Administrators (Regions VIII and X)
  • State governors (Montana, Wyoming, Idaho)
  • NPS Incident Management community
  • Hospital and utility executives in gateway towns
  • Multi-state Unified Command stakeholders authorized to activate the plan, pre-stage resources, and execute it if the volcano awakens
  • Secondary audience: Congress and state legislatures funding the USD 200 million planning envelope

Project Overview: Operational Framework

Zone Zero (the park) contains approximately 35,800 people: 35,000 tourists and 800 park staff. They must clear three designated exits—West (via West Yellowstone), North (via Gardiner), and East (toward Cody)—by T+6 hours.

Zone One extends 100 km and includes West Yellowstone (MT), Gardiner (MT), and Cody (WY). Registered residents (count not yet quantified) must evacuate by T+24 hours.

Scenario Beta activates a pre-authorized order for a 500 km ring (millions of residents) if USGS modeling indicates a 20% or higher VEI-7 probability (proposed threshold; USGS sets final values by T+3 h). This order is issued within 30 minutes of the trigger; execution proceeds in rings: 0–100 km organized evacuation, 100–250 km time-banded evacuation, 250–500 km staged departure.

Core operational elements:

  • Three contraflow corridors active by T+1 hour
  • Unified Command seated at FEMA Region VIII RRCC Denver, with FEMA Region 10 liaison from T+0 and a forward element at Livingston, MT
  • Authority handoff at park boundaries managed by a Boundary Coordination Officer
  • Pre-positioned water, N95 respirators, shelter capacity, and tow/rockfall teams
  • Multi-layered communications (IPAWS/WEA, NOAA Weather Radio, Guard satellite/radio repeaters, printed route cards in five languages)
  • Responder exposure limits: 6-hour shifts with 2-hour rest and N95 replacement; full withdrawal after 18 consecutive hours

Risks and Mitigation Strategies

  • Single-point corridor blockage: Gallatin Canyon or South Entrance closure halts outbound traffic. Mitigation: Pre-position two tow/rockfall teams with 15-minute reach; divert overflow after 45 minutes to the nearest surviving exit; abandon South Entrance after 4 hours if blockage persists.

  • Communications failure under ashfall: Cell towers fail; drivers and responders lose route guidance. Mitigation: IPAWS/WEA/NOAA Weather Radio plus National Guard satellite and radio repeaters at every control point; printed route cards in English and five additional languages (Spanish, Japanese, German, Mandarin, French).

  • Authority gaps at state boundaries: Zone expansion or reroutes stall at NPS-to-governor handoff. Mitigation: Boundary Coordination Officer at the forward Unified Command element with pre-authorized reroute protocols in signed MOUs.

  • Scenario Beta exceeds shelter capacity: The 500 km ring reaches millions of people; current plan shelters approximately 35,800. Mitigation: Ranked hub list outside the ring by T+12 hours; written plan by Month 1 (2026-11-14); signed host MOUs by Month 2 (2026-12-14).

Metrics for Success

Phase 1 (T+6 hours): At least 98% of Zone Zero evacuees (≥35,084 people) confirmed through exit counts; fewer than 716 remain under active sweep.

Phase 2 (T+24 hours):

  • At least 95% of registered Zone One residents evacuated
  • Shelters staffed and water convoys dispatched by T+12 hours; water arrival target T+24 hours via forward depots (realistic T+18-30 hours, estimate); success criterion is forward-depot pre-staging of 200,000-300,000 L (estimate)
  • Scenario Beta interim destination list issued to all evacuees

Responder continuity:

  • Zero responder casualties from ash or exhaustion
  • 6-hour shift limits and relief rotation maintained through T+72 hours

Communications:

  • 90%+ of drivers confirmed receipt of route instructions
  • 100% responder interoperability across NPS, state, and Guard networks

Post-event: After-action report and full-scale exercise completed by Month 3 (2027-01-14); MOUs signed by Month 2 (2026-12-14).

Stakeholder Benefits

FEMA: Pre-positioned incident command, mutual-aid framework, and supply-chain protocols reduce activation time and post-event cost claims; Region 8/10 seam resolved before the event.

Governors: Clear authority transfer at park boundary, pre-authorized escalation to 500 km without jurisdictional disputes; life-safety and business-continuity assurance to constituents.

NPS: Operational command at T+0, ranger exposure limits enforced, backcountry accountability transparent; federal incident-management credibility enhanced.

Gateway towns and hospitals: Shelter and supply staging in advance, patient-dispersal protocols, fuel and water priority tiers guarantee continuity during ashfall.

Regional utilities: Grid-power priorities and backup-generation contracts in place.

The public: Transparent trigger criteria, multilingual alerts restore trust and reduce chaos-driven shadow evacuation.

Ethical Considerations

The plan prioritizes life preservation and equity:

  • Responder exposure limits protect the workforce from respiratory injury
  • Pre-authorized escalation removes hindsight blame on decision makers
  • Multilingual alerts and assisted transport for mobility-limited visitors ensure no person is left behind by language or disability
  • Separate responder N95 inventory protects those enabling the evacuation
  • The plan acknowledges uncertainty: a pre-authorized trigger matrix (placeholder 20% VEI-7 probability, proposed threshold; USGS sets final values by T+3 h) is to be published so governors, utilities, and the public understand the threshold
  • The plan does not promise zero casualties (eruption magnitude is uncontrollable) but commits to minimizing preventable deaths through execution discipline, supply continuity, and transparent command

Collaboration Opportunities

Inter-agency:

  • Integrate the plan with USGS Yellowstone Volcano Observatory's hazard monitoring and trigger-matrix science
  • Collaborate with FAA on ZLC/ZSE exceptions and rotary-wing medevac corridors

Regional:

  • Engage Montana, Wyoming, and Idaho emergency managers and governors to refine MOUs, authority handoffs, and mutual-aid triggers by Month 1 (2026-11-14)
  • Host tristate tabletop and full-scale exercises at Months 2 and 3 (2026-12-14, 2027-01-14)

Hospital and utility networks:

  • Partner with regional hospital systems for surge-dispersal protocols and patient-transport drills
  • Coordinate with utilities for fuel-priority tiers and backup-generation contracts

Community and concessioner:

  • Activate Xanterra and tour operators as notification channels for foreign visitors
  • Engage Bozeman, Livingston, and Idaho Falls chambers of commerce and host-community leaders on shelter siting and second-stage hub pre-positioning

Academic:

  • Collaborate with University of Montana and University of Wyoming on ashfall-modeling validation and responder fatigue protocols

Long-term Vision

This plan establishes the first operational, pre-authorized evacuation framework for a Yellowstone-scale volcanic event, serving as the model for other caldera systems (Long Valley, Campi Flegrei) and ash-hazard zones worldwide. By Month 3 (2027-01-14), the framework matures into signed MOUs, validated second-stage hubs, and a rehearsed Scenario Beta operation, making it the standard of readiness for societal-scale hazards. Over the following years, the plan feeds into National Incident Management System doctrine, FEMA Regional training, and state emergency-management curricula, extending its influence to wildfire evacuation, hurricane contraflow, and other large-scale life-safety operations. The USD 200 million planning envelope (of which the USD 47.5–87 million readiness package is an estimate) protects 35,800 lives immediately and builds institutional capacity for the next 40 years of Yellowstone's activity window, anchoring regional resilience in science-based decision rules and executed, not theoretical, logistics.

  • Sign the tristate MOUs and EMAC (Emergency Management Assistance Compact) arrangements
  • Confirm FEMA Region 10 liaison and forward Unified Command element seated at T+0
  • Harden water and convoy contracts (existing vehicles activated verbally at T+0, dispatch by T+12 h)
  • Validate the USGS trigger matrix (final values set by T+3 h)

  • Responder reserve and N95 staging
  • Communications equipment
  • Full-scale Scenario Beta exercise by Month 3 (2027-01-14)

Escalation trigger: If modeled VEI-7 probability reaches at least 20% in the remaining window (placeholder, proposed threshold; USGS values final by T+3 h), the Unified Command issues the Scenario Beta order within 30 minutes and transitions immediately to operational Scenario Beta zones and second-stage hub pre-positioning.

Goal Statement: Evacuate about 35,800 people (35,000 tourists and 800 staff) from Yellowstone Zone Zero by T+6 hours and the 100 km Zone One by T+24 hours, then sustain regional life support under ashfall, with a pre-authorized 500 km Scenario Beta order and second-stage hub plan hardened by Month 3 (2027-01-14).

SMART Criteria

  • Specific: Clear Zone Zero (35,800 people) via three contraflow exits by T+6 hours, evacuate Zone One (West Yellowstone, Gardiner, Cody) by T+24 hours, and provide shelter, water, respiratory protection and command continuity under a Unified Command in Denver.
  • Measurable: Gate G1 at T+6: at least 98% of 35,800 confirmed through exit counts. Gate G2 at T+24: at least 95% of registered Zone One residents out, perimeter staffed, Scenario Beta interim destination list issued. Water at shelters by T+24 (target).
  • Achievable: Three exits, a Unified Command with Region 10 liaison, existing FEMA contract vehicles and Guard assets make this feasible. Pre-event lead times are not available, so readiness actions run at T+0 to T+12 hours and hardening in Months 1-3 (2026-11-14 to 2027-01-14).

  • Time-bound: Operational response from Month 0 (2026-10-14) (T+0) through T+72 hours; Zone Zero by T+6 h, Zone One by T+24 h. Scenario Beta plan, MOUs and exercises completed by Months 1-3 (2026-11-14 to 2027-01-14).

Resources Required

  • Shelter facilities at Bozeman, Idaho Falls and a third site, buses, USD 200 million planning envelope (estimate)

Related Goals

  • Regional hospital surge and power resilience

Risk Assessment and Mitigation Strategies

Key Risks

  • Single-point blockage in Gallatin Canyon or near Gardiner halts a primary corridor
  • Ash and tremor collapse cell networks, leaving drivers and responders without route guidance
  • Authority gaps at the NPS-to-state handoff and Region 8/10 seam delay reroutes
  • Scenario Beta (millions of people, not quantified) exceeds shelter, road and supply capacity with no second-stage destinations
  • Water convoys arrive T+18 to T+30 h (estimate), later than the T+12 h dispatch target

Diverse Risks

  • Responder fatigue: 100-150 rangers (estimate) leave no relief depth in the T+2 to T+8 peak
  • Ash footprint forecast error places shelters in heavy ash, forcing relocation
  • Procurement delays of 24-48 h (estimate) without pre-awarded contracts
  • Hospital and grid power loss from ash flashovers before fuel arrives
  • Conflicting shelter-in-place and evacuation messages reduce compliance and corridor throughput

Mitigation Plans

  • Pre-place at least 2 tow/rockfall teams to reach blockages within 15 min; divert overflow after 45 min (proposed threshold); loss-of-exit rule after 6 h
  • Deploy Guard signal teams, HAR/VMS and printed route cards in English plus 5 languages from T+0
  • Boundary Coordination Officer at forward element, pre-authorized state reroutes, Region 10 liaison seated at T+0
  • Interim ranked hub list outside the ring by T+12 h, tiered ring execution, written plan by Month 1 (2026-11-14), MOUs by Month 2 (2026-12-14), exercise by Month 3 (2027-01-14)
  • Forward depots, reserved convoy lane, FEMA contract vehicles with 12 h dispatch clauses; 6 h shift limits, 30-50 standby reserve, PM10 sensors and 4 h relocation rule
