  • Request additional Guard personnel from Fort Carson, Colorado or other regions if staffing demands exceed available personnel; prepare the request for UC approval if out-of-state Guard cross-deputization is needed
  • Conduct fatigue-risk assessments at T+24, T+48 and T+72 h, analyzing cumulative hours worked and recommending mandatory relief or withdrawal of personnel showing signs of critical fatigue
  • Coordinate with the three receiving hospitals (Bozeman, Livingston, Idaho Falls) to pre-stage medical support at traffic checkpoints and shelters for responder health emergencies

Initial Setup Actions:

  • Convene the board at T+0 with representatives from NPS LE, state patrol, Guard and the forward-command Safety Officer to finalize shift schedules and relief protocols
  • Count and allocate responder N95 respirators separately from the 100,000 civilian stock; confirm at least 150,000 responder+civilian N95s are available (estimate), with a 50% surge buffer for replacement cycles
  • Brief all assigned responders on exposure limits, N95 replacement protocols and mandatory withdrawal thresholds by T+0
  • Establish a 24/7 responder-fatigue hotline where personnel can report exposure symptoms, request relief, or raise concerns about unsustainable workloads
  • Confirm that the 30–50 person standby reserve is fully briefed, equipped with N95s and generator fuel, and stationed outside the ash zone and ready to deploy within 4 h

Membership:

  • NPS Chief Ranger or delegated senior safety officer (chair)
  • Forward Command Safety Officer
  • Montana Highway Patrol Incident Commander or delegated representative
  • Wyoming Highway Patrol Incident Commander or delegated representative
  • Idaho State Police Incident Commander or delegated representative
  • National Guard unit commander (regional or Fort Carson, as deployed)
  • Medical officer from the nearest receiving hospital (occupational health and emergency medicine expertise)

Decision Rights: The board has binding authority to: (1) approve or modify shift schedules and rest cycles; (2) declare any post as 'understaffed' if coverage falls below 50% due to exposure limits (proposed threshold); (3) trigger activation of the standby reserve for deployment within 4 h; (4) withdraw any individual responder from ash-exposed duty if exposure limits are breached or fatigue risk is critical; (5) recommend to the FUCE that a checkpoint be temporarily closed or consolidated with another if staffing cannot be sustained. The board does not have authority to extend exposure limits beyond the pre-written thresholds (6 h shift, 18 h withdrawal) without UC approval.

Decision Mechanism: The board meets every 6 hours during the 72-hour window (at T+0, T+6, T+12, T+18, T+24, T+30, T+36, T+42, T+48, T+54, T+60, T+66, T+72 h) to review shift logs, assess staffing adequacy and approve the next day's schedule. Decisions are made by consensus among the NPS, state and Guard commanders; if consensus fails (e.g., a state patrol commander refuses to remove an exhausted trooper from duty), the NPS Chief Ranger has final authority, with a dissent recorded for the UC. Emergency decisions (e.g., immediate withdrawal of a responder showing acute respiratory distress) are made by the board chair within 5 min and reported to the FUCE.

Meeting Cadence: Continuous 24/7 operation during the 72-hour window with formal board meetings every 6 hours (T+0, T+6, T+12 h, etc.). Ad hoc calls when a checkpoint reports staffing below 50% or a responder requests emergency relief. Daily fatigue-risk assessments at T+24, T+48 and T+72 h. Post-event responder health screening and evaluation by Month 2 (2026-12-14).

Typical Agenda Items:

  • Shift-log review: which responders worked in the past 6 h, duration, location, exposure conditions; any exposure-limit breaches; any symptomatic responders (respiratory symptoms, heat stress, confusion)
  • Staffing adequacy: current staffing vs. required staffing at each checkpoint; any posts currently unstaffed or below 50% (proposed threshold)
  • Relief rotation: which responders are due for mandatory rest; approval of next 6-hour shift schedule for all posts
  • Standby reserve deployment: current readiness status; any activation requests from the FUCE
  • N95 inventory and replacement: current stock at each checkpoint; replacement cycles (clogging rate, expected duration per mask); any shortages
  • Responder health incidents: any acute symptoms, hospital referrals or medical complications; medical follow-up recommendations

Escalation Path: Decisions about responder withdrawal or staffing shortages escalate to the FUCE Operations Section Chief, who adjusts traffic-control post assignments or consolidates posts if necessary. If staffing demands consistently exceed the available responder pool and cannot be met by the standby reserve, the board chair escalates a request for out-of-state Guard to the UC. Critical responder health emergencies (respiratory distress requiring hospitalization, heat-related collapse) are reported immediately to the nearest receiving hospital and to the UC. Any responder casualty during the event is reported to the UC and to the respective state emergency manager within 1 hour.

5. Authority & Jurisdictional Coordination Cell – Specialized Advisory (Command Clarity & Multi-State Protocol)

Rationale for Inclusion: The evacuation crosses jurisdictional boundaries between NPS (federal land), Montana, Wyoming and Idaho (state highways and communities), and FEMA Regions 8 (Denver) and 10 (Seattle), creating authority gaps and decision latency. The authority transfer is specified in writing (park boundary at each gate; NPS to state handoff), but contraflow traffic does not stop at boundaries, so vehicles and responders cross jurisdictions mid-evacuation without a clear point of responsibility handoff. A dedicated cell, co-located at the forward element with real-time links to each state's on-scene commander, owns the boundary coordination, pre-authorized reroute authority, and resolution of any NPS-state or Region 8/10 disputes. This cell prevents the 15–45 minute delays in reroute decisions that could cascade into a 500–1,000 vehicle backup.

Responsibilities:

  • Execute the written NPS-to-state authority transfer protocol at each park exit gate (West, North, East Entrance), defining the exact roadside checkpoint where NPS care ends and state custody begins; ensure both sides formally acknowledge the handoff at T+0 and throughout the evacuation
  • Authorize state on-scene commanders to issue temporary reroutes without requesting park ranger approval, pre-authorizing them at T+0 with a standing order that reroutes are valid until revoked by the FUCE
  • Manage the FEMA Region 8/10 seam: seat an explicit Region 10 liaison at the UC (Denver) by T+0 and maintain a standing mutual-aid agreement with Boise and Pocatello resource centers so that Idaho water and fuel convoys are dispatched without delay
  • Resolve any dispute between NPS and a state on-scene commander (e.g., over shelter placement, checkpoint closure or perimeter enforcement) within 30 min by convening both parties on a dedicated conference line with the Boundary Coordination Officer as mediator
  • Maintain a shared authority-transfer log (updated hourly) showing which vehicles and responders have crossed from NPS to state control at each gate, and which state now owns care for those evacuees
  • Coordinate with the FAA on airspace grounding and medevac exceptions, ensuring the Unified Command has real-time visibility into aviation restrictions and can request emergency exceptions for helicopter transport

Initial Setup Actions:

  • Brief the designated on-scene commanders for each state (Montana highway patrol at Livingston, Wyoming patrol at Cody, Idaho at Idaho Falls) on the pre-authorized reroute authority and the boundary-handoff protocol at T-6 h (before the evacuation order)
  • Establish pre-signed MOUs with Montana, Wyoming and Idaho confirming their acceptance of the UC's authority to issue Zone One and Scenario Beta evacuation orders by Month 1 (2026-11-14)
  • Issue written standing orders at T+0 granting state on-scene commanders authority to issue reroutes without seeking park ranger approval, with a dissent-reporting requirement if the commander believes a reroute violates the pre-written matrix
  • Activate the Region 10 liaison seat at the Denver RRCC by T+0 and confirm a direct phone line between the liaison and the Boise emergency management office
  • Convene a pre-event multi-state coordination exercise 60 days before the window (Month -2) to test boundary handoff, reroute decisions and mutual-aid requests under simulated congestion and ashfall scenarios

Membership:

  • Boundary Coordination Officer (forward element, chair; FEMA, NPS or Guard officer with authority to speak for the UC)
  • NPS Incident Commander or delegated zone incident commander
  • Montana Highway Patrol on-scene commander (West Yellowstone and Gardiner exits)
  • Wyoming Highway Patrol on-scene commander (Cody and East Entrance exit)
  • Idaho State Police liaison (Idaho Falls shelter coordination)
  • FEMA Region 10 liaison (seated at Denver UC or on standing conference call)
  • FAA representative or liaison (aviation grounding and medevac exceptions)

Decision Rights: The cell has binding authority to: (1) authorize state reroutes at any time without UC approval (pre-authorized standing order); (2) resolve NPS-state disputes on the fly within 30 min (Boundary Coordination Officer decision); (3) activate the Region 10 liaison's mutual-aid requests for Idaho resources without waiting for UC approval if request is below USD 5 million (proposed threshold); (4) approve helicopter medevac exceptions within the pre-authorized criteria set by the UC and FAA. The cell may not modify the written authority-transfer protocol after T+0 or unilaterally revoke a pre-authorized reroute; any such changes must escalate to the UC.

Decision Mechanism: Standing orders and pre-written authority transfers define the default decision rules, so most situations are handled without deliberation. Real-time problem-solving through a dedicated conference line: if a reroute is needed, the state commander requests it, the Boundary Coordination Officer verifies it against the pre-written matrix and authorizes it within 5 min. If an NPS ranger disputes the reroute, the matter is elevated to the Boundary Coordination Officer and the forward-element Operations Chief within 30 min for quick resolution. Tie-breaker: Boundary Coordination Officer, with escalation to the FUCE Operations Chief if the dispute creates conflicting orders.

Meeting Cadence: Continuous operation and real-time coordination during the 72-hour window via a standing conference line connecting all members. Formal briefings to the UC every 6 hours as part of the UC briefing schedule. Post-event: multi-state debrief by Month 2 (2026-12-14) with Montana, Wyoming and Idaho emergency managers to review authority handoff execution and identify improvements for future events.

Typical Agenda Items:

  • Boundary-crossing status: cumulative vehicle counts crossing from NPS to state control at each gate (West, North, East); any delays or congestion at handoff points
  • Active reroutes: which reroutes are currently in effect, which state issued them, any NPS objections or disputes, expected resolution time
  • Authority disputes: any NPS-state conflicts over shelter placement, checkpoint staffing, perimeter enforcement or other coordination issues; status of resolution efforts
  • Region 10 mutual aid: any pending requests from Idaho emergency managers for water, fuel or medical resources; dispatch status of approved requests
  • FAA coordination: any medevac exception requests, current ashfall-related airspace restrictions, anticipated exceptions for emergency helicopter transport

Escalation Path: Real-time disputes between NPS and a state are mediated by the Boundary Coordination Officer (on the standing conference line) within 30 min. If the Boundary Coordination Officer and state/NPS commanders cannot reach agreement, the matter escalates to the FUCE Operations Chief, who makes a binding decision and notifies the UC. If a state refuses to comply with a UC-authorized evacuation order, the matter escalates to the UC, which may seek legal counsel and White House involvement. Any FAA denial of a medevac exception request escalates to the UC, which may request White House or Department of Defense intervention.

6. Shelter Siting & Air-Quality Assurance Panel – Specialized Advisory (Environmental Monitoring & Dynamic Relocation Authority)

Rationale for Inclusion: The plan designates Bozeman and Idaho Falls as reception centers but acknowledges that ashfall forecasts are uncertain by 100+ km, so final shelter locations are selected at T+6 h based on the latest NOAA/USGS plume forecast. Actual ashfall may exceed model predictions by 2–3x, rendering the selected sites unsuitable and requiring emergency relocation of 10,000–15,000 evacuees within 4 h. This specialized panel owns real-time PM10 and ashfall monitoring at all shelter sites, the suitability assessment for shelter relocations, and the authority to order a relocation if thresholds are exceeded. The panel prevents the scenario in which evacuees are sheltered in heavy ash, developing respiratory distress and requiring a chaotic secondary move.

Responsibilities:

  • Maintain continuous real-time PM10 and ashfall-depth monitoring at the forward element (Livingston or Bozeman) and at all three primary shelter sites, with sensor readings updated at least hourly starting at T-12 h
  • At T+6 h, analyze the latest NOAA/USGS plume forecast (wind direction, ashfall extent, ash concentration) and recommend final shelter-site selections from the pre-surveyed candidate list; coordinate with the FUCE Operations Chief to finalize the assignments
  • Conduct ongoing suitability assessments at T+12, T+24, T+36, T+48, T+60 and T+72 h: compare current PM10 readings and ashfall forecast to the occupancy and air-filtration capacity of each primary shelter; flag any site exceeding PM10 thresholds (proposed: 50 ug/m3 for forecast update, 100 ug/m3 for suitability review)
  • If a primary shelter exceeds PM10 thresholds, initiate a rapid relocation analysis (decision within 30 min): assess ranked backup shelter sites (50+ km upwind) for suitability; prepare a relocation order and transport plan for FUCE approval
  • Issue a relocation order (within 4 h of threshold exceedance, proposed threshold) specifying the new shelter site, transport routing, and pickup schedule for the affected evacuees; track relocation logistics and confirm arrival at the new site
  • Coordinate with the supplemental N95 reserve hub (Billings or Salt Lake City) to increase N95 distribution to shelters if average daily consumption exceeds 20% of stock (proposed threshold), indicating heavier-than-modeled ashfall

Initial Setup Actions:

  • Conduct a pre-event air-quality monitoring exercise with NOAA and USGS 30 days before the window, testing real-time sensor deployment, data transmission, forecast-update protocols and relocation-decision latency
  • Pre-survey and document 8–10 candidate shelter sites across Montana, Wyoming and Idaho (Bozeman, Livingston, Billings, Idaho Falls, Sun Valley, Missoula, Cheyenne, etc.), with capacity, HVAC and filtration specs for each; rank them by distance from Yellowstone and upwind position relative to forecast wind patterns
  • Establish PM10 monitoring equipment at the forward element and at all three primary shelter sites by T-48 h, with backup sensors and battery/generator power; test satellite data transmission to ensure hourly updates are received
  • Brief shelter operators and the FUCE Operations Chief on the PM10 thresholds (50 ug/m3 for forecast update, 100 ug/m3 for suitability review) and on the relocation trigger and timeline by T-12 h
  • Confirm transport agreements (buses, drivers) for 10,000–15,000 evacuee relocation within 4 h; pre-position the buses at primary shelter sites or within 30 min drive time by T+6 h

Membership:

  • NOAA Ashfall & Air-Quality Forecast Lead (chair, real-time plume modeling and PM10 prediction)
  • USGS Geochemist or volcanologist (ashfall composition and settling-rate estimates)
  • EPA air-quality specialist (PM10 sensor calibration and air-quality standards interpretation)
  • Forward-Element Planning Chief or designee (FUCE liaison, logistical feasibility assessment for relocation)
  • Shelter Operations Coordinator (primary and backup shelter capacity and readiness)

Decision Rights: The panel has advisory authority on shelter suitability (recommendation to FUCE) and binding authority to: (1) declare that PM10 thresholds have been exceeded at a shelter site; (2) trigger the start of a relocation analysis; (3) confirm that a ranked backup shelter is suitable for occupancy and relocation can proceed; (4) recommend an increase in N95 distribution from the supplemental reserve. The final relocation order is issued by the FUCE Operations Chief, not the panel, but the panel's threshold declaration is binding and cannot be overridden by the FUCE without UC approval.

Decision Mechanism: Automated threshold alerts: when hourly PM10 readings exceed the 50 ug/m3 forecast-update threshold, an alert is triggered and the panel convenes to update the plume forecast and assess suitability. When PM10 exceeds the 100 ug/m3 suitability-review threshold (proposed), a rapid relocation analysis is triggered. The panel (NOAA, USGS and EPA members) votes on whether the current site is still safe for occupancy; a 2-out-of-3 vote determines the recommendation. The FUCE Operations Chief then decides within 1 h whether to order relocation. If the FUCE Operations Chief overrides a panel suitability finding, this override is escalated to the UC.

Meeting Cadence: Continuous real-time monitoring with automated alerts when thresholds are approached. Formal briefings to the FUCE Operations Chief every 6 hours (at the standard FUCE briefing times: T+0, T+6, T+12, T+18, T+24, etc.). Ad hoc emergency meetings when PM10 exceeds the forecast-update threshold (50 ug/m3 proposed). Post-event: joint evaluation with USGS, NOAA and EPA by Month 2 (2026-12-14) to assess forecast accuracy and identify sensor improvements.

Typical Agenda Items:

  • Hourly PM10 and ashfall-depth readings at all shelter sites and the forward element; comparison to modeled expectations
  • NOAA 72-hour plume forecast update: wind direction, ashfall extent, estimated PM10 concentrations at candidate shelter sites
  • Suitability assessment: is each primary shelter still suitable for occupancy given current and forecast ashfall; any backup sites requiring activation
  • Relocation logistics: if relocation is triggered, which backup site is recommended; transport plan and ETA for evacuee pickup and arrival
  • N95 consumption and reserve status: actual daily consumption vs. modeled expectation; any triggers for supplemental-reserve activation

Escalation Path: Suitability assessments and PM10 threshold declarations go directly to the FUCE Operations Chief, who has 1 h to decide on relocation. If the FUCE Operations Chief does not order relocation within 1 h of a panel finding that PM10 exceeds the 100 ug/m3 threshold (proposed), the panel has the right to escalate the non-response to the UC. Disputes among panel members (e.g., NOAA and USGS disagree on the forecast) are resolved by majority vote; if 2-out-of-3 cannot agree, the matter escalates to the UC with both positions documented. Critical relocation logistics failures (buses unavailable, transport gridlock) escalate to the FUCE Logistics Chief and then to the UC.

Governance Implementation Plan

1. Project Sponsor (FEMA Regional Administrator, Region VIII) and NPS Director jointly issue a written decision memo designating the Yellowstone Caldera eruption response as a 'pre-event emergency planning initiative' and authorizing the formation of a Unified Command structure. The memo names the FEMA Region VIII IC as the Unified Command chair and directs all agencies to cooperate on governance setup by Month 0 (2026-10-14). This memo serves as the legal authority to form all downstream governance bodies.

Responsible Body/Role: FEMA Regional Administrator (Region VIII) and NPS Director (joint decision authority)

Suggested Timeframe: Month -1

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Signed decision memo authorizing Unified Command formation and inter-agency cooperation
  • Named chair of the Unified Command (FEMA Region VIII IC)
  • Distribution list of required attendees and their home agencies

Dependencies:

  • Yellowstone eruption scenario and 72-hour window identified by USGS
  • Strategic decision on command structure (Unified Command at Denver RRCC with forward element at Livingston/Bozeman) approved by FEMA and NPS
  • Initial internal governance bodies list provided (4-6 bodies defined in prior phase)

2. FEMA Region VIII Incident Commander (designated UC Chair) or designee drafts a written Terms of Reference (ToR) for the Unified Command, defining its strategic authority, decision rights (zone expansion, escalation triggers, resource allocation >USD 10M), meeting cadence (continuous during 72-hour window, hourly briefings at T+0/2/6/12/24/36/48/60/72h), membership (FEMA Region VIII IC, Region 10 liaison, NPS IC, three state emergency managers/governors' designees, USGS volcanologist, NOAA forecast lead) and escalation path (tie-breaker: FEMA Region VIII IC; constitutional/legal disputes to U.S. Attorney and White House). The draft establishes the UC as a standing body that activates at T+0 and operates continuously through T+72h.

Responsible Body/Role: FEMA Region VIII Incident Commander (future UC Chair) with input from NPS, state emergency management offices and FEMA Region 10

Suggested Timeframe: Month -1, Week 2

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Draft Unified Command Terms of Reference v0.1 (15-20 pages)
  • Defined strategic decision rights and escalation paths
  • Preliminary membership list with agency confirmations

Dependencies:

  • Decision memo from FEMA RA and NPS Director issued
  • Strategic choices finalized (UC at Denver with forward element at Livingston/Bozeman)
  • FEMA Region 10 (Seattle) director identified and notified of expected liaison role

3. FEMA Region VIII Incident Commander circulates the draft UC Terms of Reference to all nominated members (NPS Director, three state emergency managers, FEMA Region 10 liaison, USGS and NOAA leads) for review and feedback. A 1-week review window is provided. Feedback is consolidated into a summary document and shared back to all reviewers, along with a revision tracker.

Responsible Body/Role: FEMA Region VIII Incident Commander (document circulation and feedback consolidation)

Suggested Timeframe: Month -1, Week 3

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • UC ToR v0.1 distributed to 9-12 stakeholders via email and secure portal
  • Individual feedback submissions from each reviewer (consolidated into a Feedback Summary)
  • Revision tracker showing which comments have been incorporated

Dependencies:

  • Draft UC ToR v0.1 completed
  • Contact list of all nominated members with email addresses and office secure-portal access confirmed

4. FEMA Region VIII Incident Commander revises the UC ToR based on consolidated feedback and issues UC ToR v1.0 (final). Key revisions may include: (1) clarification of Region 10 liaison's voting rights on Idaho-specific decisions; (2) formalizing the 'veto override' protocol (each state governor has one veto; majority rule after override used); (3) defining the shared common operating picture (COP) digital dashboard and update frequency (hourly). The final ToR is signed by the FEMA Region VIII IC and submitted to the FEMA Regional Administrator for official approval.

Responsible Body/Role: FEMA Region VIII Incident Commander with final sign-off from FEMA Regional Administrator

Suggested Timeframe: Month -1, Week 4

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Unified Command Terms of Reference v1.0 (final, signed)
  • FEMA Regional Administrator approval letter
  • Decision log documenting which feedback was incorporated and why

Dependencies:

  • UC ToR v0.1 and consolidated Feedback Summary completed
  • Revisions approved by FEMA Region VIII IC

5. FEMA Region VIII Incident Commander issues formal written appointment letters to each nominated member of the Unified Command, confirming their role, decision rights and the time commitment (continuous operation from T+0 to T+72h, then ongoing Months 1-3 = 2026-11-14 to 2027-01-14 for MOUs and exercises). Letters are sent to the home agencies (NPS, three states, FEMA Region 10, USGS, NOAA) with a request for verbal confirmation of acceptance within 48 hours. Any rejections or substitute nominees are flagged for resolution by the FEMA Regional Administrator.

Responsible Body/Role: FEMA Region VIII Incident Commander (letter issuance)

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Week 1 (Days -7 to 0 before T+0 on 2026-10-14)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Formal appointment letters to 9-12 UC members (signed by FEMA Region VIII IC)
  • Confirmation of acceptance from each member's home agency (email or memo)
  • Roster of confirmed UC membership with titles and contact information

Dependencies:

  • UC ToR v1.0 final and approved
  • Contact information for all nominated members and their supervisors

6. FEMA Region VIII Incident Commander or designee holds a pre-event UC 'Orientation and Authority Briefing' meeting (in-person or virtual hybrid) for all confirmed UC members. The briefing covers: (1) the pre-authorized USGS trigger matrix for Scenario Beta (VEI-7 indicators, thresholds to be finalized by T+3h); (2) the three-exit contraflow plan and the 45-minute blockage-diversion rule (proposed threshold); (3) the Authority & Jurisdictional Cell's role in the NPS-to-state handoff; (4) the COP digital dashboard demo and how to access it; (5) the continuous briefing schedule (T+0, T+2, T+6, T+12, T+24, etc.). A Q&A session addresses any ambiguities in decision rights or escalation paths. All attendees sign an acknowledgment of understanding.

Responsible Body/Role: FEMA Region VIII Incident Commander (host and facilitator) with support from NPS IC and state emergency managers

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Week 2 (Days -7 to -1 before T+0)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • UC Orientation briefing agenda and slides
  • Pre-authorized USGS trigger-matrix summary (preliminary; final thresholds by T+3h)
  • COP dashboard access credentials for all UC members
  • Signed attendance roster and acknowledgment-of-understanding forms

Dependencies:

  • UC ToR v1.0 final and all members confirmed
  • USGS preliminary trigger-matrix indicators (uplift rate, seismic magnitude, magma depth) identified
  • COP digital platform and dashboard deployed and tested

7. FEMA Region VIII Incident Commander formally activates the Unified Command at T+0 (2026-10-14, coinciding with the eruption alert and evacuation order from the project sponsor). All UC members report to their designated seats at the FEMA Region VIII RRCC in Denver (remote participation accepted for state emergency managers if in-person travel is not feasible). The UC chair convenes the first formal briefing, reviews the COP dashboard status (expected: ~0 evacuees out at T+0, all exit corridors open, ashfall not yet detected), and confirms that all five specialized advisory bodies (Escalation Cell, FUCE, Responder Health Board, Authority Cell, Shelter Siting Panel) are standing by and ready to accept delegated authority from the UC.

Responsible Body/Role: Unified Command (led by FEMA Region VIII IC)

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hour 0 (2026-10-14, T+0)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • UC formally activated memo (signed by FEMA Region VIII IC)
  • First UC briefing held; meeting minutes documenting status of evacuation corridors, supply convoys, responder deployment, and advisory-body readiness
  • COP dashboard populated with baseline data (evacuation gates open, no blockages, no ashfall yet, all exit corridors confirmed passable)

Dependencies:

  • Evacuation order issued by project sponsor (NPS and FEMA)
  • All UC members confirmed ready and in position at T+0
  • FUCE, Escalation Cell and advisory bodies staffed and standing by

8. Forward Unified Command Element (FUCE) senior staff (Operations Chief, Logistics Chief, Planning Chief, Safety Officer, Boundary Coordination Officer, Guard Signal Officer and USGS/NOAA liaisons) meet at the forward command element location (Livingston, MT, or alternate Bozeman) by T+1 hour to formally establish the FUCE as an operational entity under the UC. The Operations Chief briefs the team on the delegated authority (traffic management, tow dispatch, water convoy routing, shelter relocation triggers within pre-authorized rules) and confirms that communication links to the UC in Denver are live and tested. All FUCE members acknowledge their roles and confirm readiness to execute continuous operations until T+72h.

Responsible Body/Role: FUCE Operations Section Chief (incident commander for forward operations)

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hours 0–1 (T+0 to T+1)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • FUCE formally established at Livingston (or Bozeman) location
  • FUCE organization chart and role assignments (Operations, Logistics, Planning, Safety, Boundary Coordination, Signal, liaisons)
  • Communication test between FUCE and UC Denver (voice, data, COP dashboard access confirmed)
  • FUCE initial briefing minutes documenting status of control points, tow teams, water convoy readiness

Dependencies:

  • UC formally activated
  • Livingston command facility (or Bozeman backup) prepared with communications equipment, desks, COP displays and generator backup
  • All FUCE section chiefs confirmed in position

9. Escalation & Scenario Beta Decision Cell (USGS Volcano Disaster Assistance Program lead, USGS seismologist, USGS magma modeler, NOAA forecast lead, and UC liaison) convene at T+0 at either the FUCE location (Livingston) or the UC location (Denver RRCC), as coordinated. The cell chair (USGS Disaster Assistance Program lead) reviews the pre-authorized USGS trigger matrix (preliminary, to be finalized by T+3h using real-time USGS data) and establishes live monitoring of USGS seismic, GPS and gas networks. The cell confirms that data feeds are arriving in real time and that automated threshold alerts are armed. The cell also briefs the UC liaison on the status of each eruption indicator relative to the Scenario Beta trigger threshold.

Responsible Body/Role: Escalation & Scenario Beta Decision Cell (led by USGS Volcano Disaster Assistance Program lead)

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hour 0 (T+0)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Escalation Cell formally established and operational
  • Live USGS data feeds (seismic, GPS, gas) confirmed arriving at monitoring station (FUCE or UC)
  • Preliminary trigger-matrix thresholds defined (uplift rate, seismic magnitude, magma depth); final thresholds to be confirmed by T+3h
  • Automated threshold-alert system armed; decision log created for documenting indicator values hourly
  • Initial briefing to UC: current status of each indicator relative to the Scenario Beta trigger

Dependencies:

  • UC formally activated
  • USGS real-time monitoring network operational (seismic, GPS, gas)
  • Live data-feed connections to the FUCE or UC command center confirmed

10. Responder Health & Fatigue Management Board (NPS Chief Ranger, Forward Command Safety Officer, state highway patrol commanders for MT/WY/ID, National Guard unit commander, and medical officer from the nearest receiving hospital) convene at T+0 at the FUCE or a nearby regional coordination center. The board chair (NPS Chief Ranger) reviews the pre-written exposure limits (6-hour shifts at ash-exposed posts, 2-hour rest with N95 replacement, 18-hour withdrawal threshold) and confirms that all assigned responders have been briefed on these limits and on the fatigue-hotline contact information. The board also confirms that the 30–50 person standby reserve is stationed outside the ash zone and ready to deploy within 4 hours if staffing falls below 50% at any checkpoint.

Responsible Body/Role: Responder Health & Fatigue Management Board (led by NPS Chief Ranger)

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hour 0 (T+0)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Responder Health Board formally established and operational
  • Exposure limits briefing memo issued to all assigned responders (rangers, patrol officers, Guard)
  • Responder N95 inventory confirmed (counted separately from 100,000 civilian stock); total estimated 150,000–200,000 with 50% surge buffer
  • Fatigue-hotline contact information distributed to all responders
  • Standby reserve roster confirmed (30–50 personnel stationed outside ash zone, ready to deploy)
  • Initial board briefing minutes documenting responder deployment status and shift assignments for the first 6 hours

Dependencies:

  • FUCE formally established
  • All responder positions (rangers, patrol, Guard) assigned and confirmed
  • Standby reserve personnel identified, briefed and pre-positioned outside the ash zone

11. Authority & Jurisdictional Coordination Cell (Boundary Coordination Officer at the FUCE, NPS IC or delegated zone commander, MT/WY/ID highway patrol and state police on-scene commanders, FEMA Region 10 liaison, and FAA representative) convene at T+0 to formally establish the cell and activate the authority-transfer protocols. The Boundary Coordination Officer briefs all members on the pre-written NPS-to-state handoff protocol at each park exit gate (West, North, East Entrance), confirming that state on-scene commanders have been pre-authorized to issue reroutes without park ranger approval (standing order, pre-signed by the UC chair). The Region 10 liaison confirms that FEMA Region 10 mutual-aid arrangements with Boise and Pocatello emergency management offices are documented in a standing MOU to be finalized by Month 1 (2026-11-14).

Responsible Body/Role: Authority & Jurisdictional Coordination Cell (led by Boundary Coordination Officer at FUCE)

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hour 0 (T+0)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Authority Cell formally established and operational at FUCE
  • NPS-to-state authority-transfer protocol memo re-issued to all members (West, North, East Entrance gates; roadside checkpoints defined)
  • Standing order authorizing state on-scene reroutes without park approval (signed by UC chair, signed by each state emergency manager)
  • Authority-transfer log template created (hourly updates tracking vehicle and responder crossings at each gate)
  • Region 10 liaison confirmed in position at Denver UC; preliminary mutual-aid contacts from Boise and Pocatello confirmed
  • FAA liaison confirmed in position; aviation-grounding procedure and medevac-exception criteria reviewed

Dependencies:

  • UC formally activated
  • FUCE established with Boundary Coordination Officer in position
  • Written NPS-to-state handoff protocol drafted and pre-reviewed by all states
  • Region 10 liaison identified and contact information confirmed

12. Shelter Siting & Air-Quality Assurance Panel (NOAA ashfall/air-quality forecast lead, USGS geochemist, EPA air-quality specialist, FUCE Planning Chief, and Shelter Operations Coordinator) convene at T+0 at the FUCE location. The panel chair (NOAA lead) confirms that real-time PM10 and ashfall-depth monitoring sensors are deployed at the forward element (Livingston) and at the three primary shelter candidates (Bozeman, Idaho Falls, and a third site to be determined based on the T+6 forecast). The panel reviews the pre-surveyed list of 8–10 backup candidate shelters (ranked by distance and upwind position) and confirms that transport agreements (buses, drivers) are in place for emergency relocation of 10,000–15,000 evacuees within 4 hours.

Responsible Body/Role: Shelter Siting & Air-Quality Assurance Panel (led by NOAA ashfall/air-quality forecast lead)

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hour 0 (T+0)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Shelter Siting Panel formally established and operational at FUCE
  • Real-time PM10 and ashfall-depth monitoring confirmed at forward element and all primary shelter sites; automated alerts armed (thresholds: 50 ug/m³ forecast-update trigger, 100 ug/m³ suitability-review trigger)
  • Pre-surveyed backup shelter sites list (8–10 candidates) with capacity, HVAC and filtration specs for each
  • Transport agreements for rapid relocation (buses, drivers confirmed) within 4 hours of relocation order
  • Initial briefing to UC: current ashfall forecast and modeled ash extent for the 72-hour window

Dependencies:

  • FUCE formally established
  • PM10 monitoring sensors deployed and tested at forward element and shelter sites
  • NOAA plume model and forecast data feeding into real-time dashboard
  • Backup shelter sites pre-surveyed by Month -1

13. UC holds the formal first Unified Command briefing at T+0, with participation by all six UC members (or their confirmed delegates) and representatives from all five specialized advisory bodies (Escalation Cell, FUCE, Responder Health Board, Authority Cell, Shelter Siting Panel). The agenda includes: (1) status of evacuation corridors and gate operations (target 0 departures at T+0, ramping to flow rate of ~2,000 vehicles/hour by T+1); (2) summary of USGS eruption indicators and distance from the Scenario Beta trigger (provided by Escalation Cell); (3) current ashfall forecast and PM10 readings (provided by Shelter Siting Panel); (4) readiness status of water convoys (target dispatch from Salt Lake City by T+12h) and supply logistics (provided by FUCE Logistics Chief); (5) responder staffing and exposure-limit compliance (provided by Responder Health Board); (6) authority-transfer protocols and any initial boundary-coordination issues (provided by Authority Cell). A shared common operating picture (COP) digital dashboard is displayed and updated continuously during the briefing, showing all metrics hourly.

Responsible Body/Role: Unified Command (led by FEMA Region VIII IC, chair)

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hour 0–2 (T+0 to T+2)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • UC First Briefing agenda and slide deck
  • Briefing minutes documenting: evacuation gate status, USGS indicator status, ashfall forecast, supply convoy readiness, responder deployment, and authority-transfer protocol execution
  • COP digital dashboard snapshot (baseline T+0 data)
  • UC decision log initiated (documenting any real-time decisions, tie-breakers or escalations)
  • Attendee roster (UC members and advisors confirmed present or remote)

Dependencies:

  • UC formally activated
  • All five specialized advisory bodies established and operational
  • COP digital dashboard live and populated with baseline data
  • USGS, NOAA, FUCE, Responder Health Board and Authority Cell ready to brief

14. USGS Volcano Disaster Assistance Program lead (Escalation Cell chair) completes the refinement of the pre-authorized USGS trigger matrix using the latest real-time eruption-monitoring data (seismic swarm, GPS uplift, gas emissions, magma-depth models) available at T+3h. The cell finalizes the specific numerical thresholds for: (1) uplift rate (cm/h or cm/6h intervals); (2) seismic-swarm magnitude and frequency triggers; (3) gas-flux thresholds (SO2, CO2); (4) estimated magma depth and ascent rate indicating VEI-7 probability ≥20% in the remaining window (placeholder; USGS to provide exact formula). The finalized matrix is issued in writing and distributed to the UC, FUCE, and all state emergency managers. A dashboard showing the current status of each indicator relative to the finalized trigger thresholds is published and made available to the media and the public to ensure credibility and transparency.

Responsible Body/Role: Escalation & Scenario Beta Decision Cell (led by USGS Volcano Disaster Assistance Program lead)

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hour 3 (T+3h)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Finalized USGS trigger-matrix document (signed by USGS Disaster Assistance Program lead)
  • Specific numerical thresholds for uplift rate, seismic magnitude, gas flux and magma-depth estimates
  • Decision-dashboard snapshot showing current indicator values relative to finalized thresholds
  • Trigger-matrix distribution memo to UC, FUCE, states and media
  • Public-facing summary of the trigger matrix explaining how Scenario Beta escalation works

Dependencies:

  • Escalation Cell established at T+0
  • Real-time USGS data feeds live and streaming continuously
  • Preliminary matrix indicators identified at T+0

15. FUCE Operations Chief and FEMA logistics coordinator confirm that contraflow traffic-control operations are active on all three exit corridors (US-20/US-191 via Gallatin Canyon to West Yellowstone, US-89 via Gardiner, US-14/16/20 toward Cody) by T+1 hour. Traffic-control posts are staffed at each corridor (rangers, highway patrol, and National Guard at key junctions and bottlenecks). At least two tow and rockfall-clearance teams are deployed to pre-positioned stations (Mammoth and Spanish Creek area) and confirmed ready to reach any Gallatin Canyon blockage within 15 minutes of dispatch. Guard signal teams with satellite phones, portable repeaters and generator fuel are deployed to each control point and the forward element by T+1 hour. IPAWS (Integrated Public Alert and Warning System) messages in English and five languages (Spanish, Japanese, German, Mandarin, French) are issued to the public, instructing drivers to use designated exit corridors and to follow ranger/patrol instructions.

Responsible Body/Role: FUCE Operations Section Chief and Logistics Chief

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hour 1 (T+1h)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Confirmation that contraflow is active on all three corridors (signed statement from each state DOT or National Guard unit)
  • Traffic-control post staffing roster (rangers, patrol, Guard) for each corridor and checkpoint
  • Tow and rockfall-clearance team deployment confirmation (2+ teams at Mammoth/Spanish Creek area, ready for 15-minute response)
  • Guard signal-team deployment confirmation at all control points and forward element
  • IPAWS message distribution log (English and five languages; timestamp of broadcast and carrier confirmation)

Dependencies:

  • UC formally activated and evacuation order issued by project sponsor
  • FUCE Operations Chief in position at Livingston
  • Tow teams and Guard signal teams pre-positioned or nearby and ready to deploy

16. Shelter Siting Panel conducts the formal selection of final shelter sites at T+6 hours, using the latest NOAA/USGS plume forecast and real-time PM10 monitoring data. The panel reviews the ashfall-extent forecast, wind direction and ash-concentration projections for the next 72 hours. Based on this forecast, the panel recommends primary and backup shelter sites that lie outside or upwind of the modeled ash footprint. The FUCE Operations Chief formally approves the shelter-site selections and issues assignments to the Bozeman and Idaho Falls shelters (or alternates if the forecast indicates those sites are unsuitable). Buses and intake staff are dispatched to the selected sites to prepare for receiving the first evacuees (expected arrival T+6 to T+12h).

Responsible Body/Role: Shelter Siting & Air-Quality Assurance Panel (led by NOAA forecast lead) with final approval by FUCE Operations Chief

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hour 6 (T+6h)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Final shelter-site selection recommendation from the Shelter Siting Panel (with ashfall-forecast justification)
  • PM10 and ashfall-depth readings at all candidate sites at T+6h
  • FUCE approval memo for final shelter assignments
  • Shelter intake and operations teams dispatched and confirmation of arrival at selected sites
  • Briefing to UC documenting the shelter-siting decision and any deviations from the pre-planned Bozeman/Idaho Falls locations

Dependencies:

  • Shelter Siting Panel established and monitoring active at T+0
  • Real-time PM10 sensors at all candidate sites
  • NOAA plume forecast updated at T+6h

17. UC issues a milestone assessment at T+6 hours, checking against the Phase 1 'go/no-go' gate: at least 98% of the 35,800 Zone Zero evacuees (about 35,084) have been counted as having exited through the three corridors (West, North, East gates). Real-time exit counts from each state patrol and NPS checkpoint are consolidated in the COP dashboard. If the gate is met, the UC documents clearance and advises that Zone Zero is essentially cleared, with remaining stragglers (estimated 200–400 backcountry hikers and permit holders) under active ranger sweep and accounting. If the gate is not met (e.g., due to a blockage that delayed departures), the UC convenes an emergency reroute decision with the FUCE and Authority Cell to redirect any remaining vehicles and assess whether the 72-hour window timeline needs adjustment.

Responsible Body/Role: Unified Command (led by FEMA Region VIII IC) with real-time data from FUCE and state checkpoints

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hour 6 (T+6h)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Phase 1 Gate G1 assessment document (yes/no decision: at least 98% of 35,800 confirmed out)
  • Cumulative exit counts by corridor (West, North, East) at T+6h
  • List of any remaining unaccounted-for parties (backcountry, lodges, permit holders); status of ranger sweeps
  • UC briefing documenting gate results and any reroute or staffing adjustments triggered by shortfalls
  • COP dashboard snapshot at T+6h showing gate status, ashfall conditions and shelter readiness

Dependencies:

  • Contraflow operations active on all three corridors from T+0 to T+6
  • Real-time exit counting and reporting from state checkpoints and NPS
  • FUCE and Authority Cell coordinating reroutes and gate-status reporting

18. UC issues a formal public statement and IPAWS alert at T+6 hours, confirming that Zone Zero (park interior) has been cleared or is nearly cleared, and that the evacuation is transitioning to Phase 2: expansion of Zone One (100 km radius including West Yellowstone, Gardiner and Cody communities). The statement reiterates the pre-authorized USGS trigger matrix and explains that if the triggers for Scenario Beta (VEI-7) are detected, a 500 km evacuation order will be issued immediately without further deliberation. The statement also confirms current shelter locations (Bozeman, Idaho Falls and any third site), water convoy dispatch status (target T+12h from Salt Lake City), and the N95 pre-staging locations. This public statement is critical for sustaining public trust and explaining the escalation logic before Scenario Beta messaging may become necessary.

Responsible Body/Role: Unified Command (FEMA Region VIII IC) in coordination with NOAA Public Affairs and NPS Communications

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hour 6 (T+6h)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • UC public statement confirming Phase 1 clearance and Zone One expansion (signed by FEMA Region VIII IC)
  • IPAWS alert in English and five languages explaining Scenario Beta trigger logic and shelter locations
  • Media briefing slides and talking points for state and federal public affairs
  • Confirmation of broadcast on local radio, TV and social-media channels

Dependencies:

  • Phase 1 Gate G1 assessment complete
  • Shelter siting decisions finalized
  • USGS trigger matrix finalized and published

19. FEMA Region VIII IC (UC chair) or designee issues written pre-authorization letters to each of the three state governors (Montana, Wyoming, Idaho), requesting verbal confirmation of their authorization of the UC's Zone One and Scenario Beta (500 km) evacuation orders. The letters explain: (1) the current status of the evacuation (Phase 1 complete, Zone One now being evacuated); (2) the pre-written USGS trigger matrix and how Scenario Beta will be triggered if thresholds are crossed; (3) the request for each governor to confirm that they accept the UC's authority to issue and enforce these orders on state highways and in state communities; (4) the expectation that formal Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) and EMAC mutual-aid agreements will be signed by Month 1 (2026-11-14). Verbal confirmations are recorded and documented in the UC decision log.

Responsible Body/Role: FEMA Region VIII IC (UC chair) on behalf of the Unified Command

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hour 6 (T+6h)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Pre-authorization letters issued to MT, WY and ID governors (transmitted via secure fax and secure email)
  • Verbal confirmations recorded and transcribed (audio or written summary)
  • UC decision-log entries documenting each governor's confirmation (or any objections/conditions)
  • Schedule confirmed for signing formal MOUs by Month 1 (2026-11-14)

Dependencies:

  • Zone One evacuation order issued by project sponsor (NPS and FEMA)
  • Phase 1 Gate G1 assessment complete
  • USGS trigger matrix finalized

20. FUCE Logistics Chief confirms that bottled-water convoys from Salt Lake City distribution centers have been dispatched by T+12 hours (per the T+12h target), using National Guard escorts and reserved lanes on I-15 northbound (proposed dedicated 'supply-surge' lane). The Logistics Chief tracks the real-time location of each convoy via GPS and reports arrival estimates at Bozeman and Idaho Falls shelters. If the forecast arrival time exceeds T+24h (the Phase 2 gate deadline), the Logistics Chief alerts the FUCE Operations Chief and the UC, triggering contingency actions: (1) advance dispatch of supplemental water from forward depots in Bozeman, Billings and Idaho Falls (pre-positioned at T-48 hours before the event); (2) activation of the supplemental N95 reserve at Billings or Salt Lake City if ashfall is heavier than modeled.

Responsible Body/Role: FUCE Logistics Section Chief

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hour 12 (T+12h)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Water-convoy dispatch confirmation from Salt Lake City (signed order, timestamp, carrier confirmation)
  • Convoy tracking (GPS coordinates, real-time location updates, ETA at Bozeman and Idaho Falls)
  • Contingency activation decision (if ETA >T+24h): order for forward-depot supplemental water and supplemental N95 deployment
  • Briefing to FUCE and UC documenting water-supply status and any logistics adjustments

Dependencies:

  • FUCE Logistics Chief in position
  • Water-supply contracts with pre-authorized 12-hour dispatch clauses in place (signed before Month 0 = 2026-10-14)
  • Forward depots at Bozeman, Billings and Idaho Falls pre-stocked with water and N95 by T-48h

21. Authority Cell conducts a formal review of authority-transfer and jurisdictional-coordination execution at T+12 hours. The Boundary Coordination Officer consolidates reports from all three state on-scene commanders (MT at West/Gardiner, WY at Cody, ID at Idaho Falls) documenting: (1) cumulative vehicle and evacuee counts that have crossed from NPS to state control at each boundary checkpoint; (2) any reroutes or traffic-control adjustments issued by state commanders (all within pre-authorized standing orders); (3) any disputes or coordination gaps that required escalation to the FUCE or UC. The cell issues a brief status report to the UC confirming that the authority transfer is executing smoothly or flagging any issues requiring UC decision-making.

Responsible Body/Role: Authority & Jurisdictional Coordination Cell (led by Boundary Coordination Officer)

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hour 12 (T+12h)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Authority-transfer execution report from Boundary Coordination Officer
  • Cumulative authority-transfer log (vehicles and responders crossing from NPS to state control at each gate)
  • Summary of reroutes issued by state on-scene commanders (all within standing authorization)
  • Any disputes or escalations identified and the resolution
  • Briefing to FUCE and UC documenting jurisdictional-coordination status

Dependencies:

  • Authority Cell established at T+0
  • Standing orders authorizing state reroutes issued at T+0
  • State on-scene commanders in position at their respective gates and checkpoints

22. Responder Health Board conducts a mandatory 6-hour fatigue-risk assessment at T+12 hours, analyzing cumulative hours worked by all assigned responders (rangers, patrol, Guard at traffic-control and perimeter posts) since T+0. The board reviews shift logs and identifies any responders approaching or exceeding the 18-hour withdrawal threshold (proposed threshold). Any responders exceeding 6 hours at ash-exposed posts without a 2-hour rest break are flagged for immediate rotation. The board also tallies N95 mask usage and confirms that inventory is adequate for the next 12 hours. If usage is exceeding expectations (e.g., heavy ashfall causing faster mask clogging), the board signals the FUCE Logistics Chief to activate supplemental responder N95 reserves.

Responsible Body/Role: Responder Health & Fatigue Management Board (led by NPS Chief Ranger)

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hour 12 (T+12h)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Responder fatigue-risk assessment report documenting cumulative hours worked by all deployed responders
  • List of responders exceeding exposure limits or requiring immediate rotation
  • N95 inventory and consumption summary (actual vs. modeled expected usage)
  • Contingency activation decision (if usage exceeding expectations)
  • Briefing to FUCE and UC with staffing-continuity recommendations

Dependencies:

  • Responder Health Board established at T+0
  • Shift logs maintained at all traffic-control posts and forwarded to the board every 2 hours
  • N95 inventory tracked in real time at each post

23. Escalation Cell issues an Escalation Readiness Assessment at T+12 hours, reporting the current status of each USGS eruption indicator (uplift rate, seismic magnitude, gas flux, magma depth) relative to the finalized Scenario Beta trigger thresholds. The cell states how far (percentage or margin) each indicator is from the trigger and estimates the time to trigger if current trends continue. The cell also reviews the current ashfall forecast and PM10 readings, noting any changes from the T+6h forecast. This briefing is delivered to the UC and published in a summary format suitable for media and public consumption, maintaining transparency about the eruption state and the likelihood of Scenario Beta escalation.

Responsible Body/Role: Escalation & Scenario Beta Decision Cell (led by USGS Volcano Disaster Assistance Program lead)

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hour 12 (T+12h)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Escalation Readiness Assessment document (1-2 pages, signed by USGS lead)
  • Current indicator-status dashboard (snapshot of each indicator relative to finalized thresholds)
  • Estimated time-to-trigger calculation if current trends continue
  • Updated ashfall forecast and PM10 readings
  • Public-facing summary explaining the escalation status in non-technical language

Dependencies:

  • Escalation Cell established at T+0
  • USGS trigger matrix finalized by T+3h
  • Real-time USGS monitoring data streaming continuously

24. UC holds the T+12 hour formal briefing, consolidating status reports from the FUCE, all five specialized advisory bodies, and state on-scene commanders. The agenda includes: (1) Zone One evacuation progress (target: evacuees flowing into Bozeman, Idaho Falls and third shelter site; intake and registration ongoing); (2) USGS indicator status and Scenario Beta readiness; (3) ashfall forecast and shelter-suitability status (PM10 readings, any triggers for relocation analysis); (4) water convoy ETA and supply-logistics status; (5) responder fatigue and staffing continuity; (6) authority-transfer execution and any jurisdictional disputes. The UC documents any mid-course corrections needed (e.g., reroutes, shelter relocation preparations, additional Guard deployment) and issues updated orders to the FUCE and state commanders.

Responsible Body/Role: Unified Command (led by FEMA Region VIII IC, chair)

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hour 12 (T+12h)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • UC T+12h Briefing agenda and briefing minutes
  • Status summaries from FUCE, advisory bodies and states (consolidated into one briefing package)
  • COP dashboard snapshot at T+12h
  • UC decision log documenting any mid-course orders or escalations
  • Updated UC daily orders (if needed) to FUCE and state commanders

Dependencies:

  • FUCE status report prepared and submitted on time
  • All five advisory bodies prepared to brief at T+12h

25. FEMA Region VIII IC (UC chair), on behalf of the Unified Command, issues a written request to the three state governors (MT, WY, ID) and to FEMA Region 10 (Seattle) requesting formal signing of Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) and EMAC mutual-aid agreements by Month 1 (2026-11-14). The request includes draft MOU language covering: (1) each state's acceptance of the UC's authority to issue Zone One and Scenario Beta evacuation orders; (2) commitment to enforce unified evacuation messaging and shelter assignments on state roads and in state communities; (3) provision of state resources (highway patrol, National Guard) to support contraflow and perimeter operations; (4) mutual-aid resource sharing (water, fuel, medical) among the three states and with FEMA Regions 8 and 10; (5) post-event after-action-report and exercise planning for Months 1–3 (2026-11-14 to 2027-01-14). This request initiates a formal negotiation period that culminates in signed agreements by Month 1 (2026-11-14).

Responsible Body/Role: FEMA Region VIII IC (UC chair) on behalf of the Unified Command

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hours 24–36 (T+24h to T+36h)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • MOU and EMAC agreement request letters issued to MT, WY and ID governors and FEMA Region 10
  • Draft MOU and EMAC language (attached to request letters)
  • Schedule for MOU-signature meetings (targeted completion by Month 1, 2026-11-14)
  • UC decision-log entry documenting issuance of MOU requests

Dependencies:

  • Verbal governor authorizations obtained at T+6h
  • Unified Command operations progressing smoothly
  • No major disputes or coordination gaps between NPS and states

26. UC issues a milestone assessment at T+24 hours, checking against the Phase 2 'go/no-go' gate: at least 95% of registered Zone One residents (West Yellowstone, Gardiner, Cody communities) have evacuated or sheltered in place, perimeters around evacuated towns are staffed and secured by National Guard to prevent looting, and a preliminary Scenario Beta interim-destination list (ranked hub list outside the 500 km ring) has been issued. The UC consolidates reports from the FUCE, state on-scene commanders and the Shelter Siting Panel, documenting evacuation completeness, perimeter-staffing status and shelter-intake progress. If the gate is met, the UC documents successful completion of Phase 2 and advises that the response has transitioned to the 'sustained operations' phase (T+24h to T+72h), during which the focus shifts to supply continuity, ashfall management and Scenario Beta readiness.

Responsible Body/Role: Unified Command (led by FEMA Region VIII IC) with data from FUCE, state commanders and advisory bodies

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hour 24 (T+24h)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Phase 2 Gate G2 assessment document (yes/no decision: at least 95% of Zone One residents out; perimeters staffed; interim hub list issued)
  • Zone One evacuation completion report by community (West Yellowstone, Gardiner, Cody)
  • Perimeter-staffing and anti-looting operational status
  • Interim Scenario Beta hub-destination list (ranked candidates outside the 500 km ring)
  • UC briefing documenting gate results and transition to sustained-operations phase
  • COP dashboard snapshot at T+24h

Dependencies:

  • Zone One evacuation proceeding as planned from T+6h to T+24h
  • Perimeter enforcement and National Guard deployment completed
  • Scenario Beta hub preliminary list researched and drafted by planning staff

27. Shelter Siting Panel conducts formal suitability assessments at T+24, T+36, T+48, T+60 and T+72 hours, comparing real-time PM10 readings and ashfall forecasts at all active shelter sites against the established thresholds (50 ug/m³ for forecast-update trigger, 100 ug/m³ for suitability-review trigger). If any site exceeds the suitability threshold, the panel initiates a rapid relocation analysis (decision within 30 minutes proposed threshold) and recommends a backup site. A relocation order (issued by FUCE Operations Chief within 4 hours of threshold exceedance proposed threshold) specifies the new shelter site, transport routing and pickup schedule. The panel tracks all relocation logistics and confirms arrival of evacuees at the new site. This continuous monitoring and rapid-response protocol prevents evacuees from being sheltered in heavy ashfall and developing respiratory distress.

Responsible Body/Role: Shelter Siting & Air-Quality Assurance Panel (led by NOAA forecast lead) with execution by FUCE Operations Chief

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hours 24, 36, 48, 60, 72 (T+24h, T+36h, T+48h, T+60h, T+72h)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Shelter-suitability assessment reports at each time interval (T+24h, T+36h, T+48h, T+60h, T+72h)
  • PM10 and ashfall-depth readings at all active and backup shelter sites
  • Any relocation analyses and recommendations
  • Relocation orders issued by FUCE Operations Chief (if suitability thresholds exceeded)
  • Transport and logistics confirmation for any relocation (buses, pickup schedule, arrival confirmation)

Dependencies:

  • Shelter Siting Panel established at T+0 with continuous PM10 monitoring
  • Real-time PM10 data streaming to the panel and FUCE
  • Backup shelter sites pre-surveyed and transport agreements in place

28. UC holds continuous hourly briefings (in addition to the scheduled T+0, T+2, T+6, T+12, T+24, T+36, T+48, T+60, T+72h formal briefings) during the 72-hour window, with rapid-update reports from the FUCE on any critical changes: corridor blockages, major weather shifts, ashfall intensity changes, supply delays or any USGS eruption-indicator changes approaching the Scenario Beta trigger threshold. These rapid-update calls (conducted via secure conference line) allow the UC to make real-time tactical decisions (reroutes, shelter relocations, supply contingencies) without waiting for the formal scheduled briefing. All UC decisions made between scheduled briefings are logged in the UC decision log with full documentation and time stamps.

Responsible Body/Role: Unified Command (led by FEMA Region VIII IC, chair) with participation by FUCE Operations Chief and key advisory-body leads as needed

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hours 0–72 (T+0 to T+72h), continuous as needed between scheduled briefings

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Rapid-update call logs (time, participants, issue discussed, decision made)
  • UC decision log entries for all decisions made on rapid-update calls
  • COP dashboard updated in real time following each rapid-update call
  • Notification memos to affected parties (states, FUCE, advisory bodies) documenting new UC orders or directives

Dependencies:

  • UC continuously staffed at the FEMA Region VIII RRCC Denver
  • FUCE Operations Chief available for rapid escalation calls 24/7
  • Secure conference-line infrastructure and communications tested

29. Escalation Cell continuously monitors real-time USGS eruption indicators throughout the 72-hour window and immediately alerts the UC if any indicator crosses 80% of the Scenario Beta trigger threshold (a warning threshold), triggering a pre-brief for the UC. If any indicator crosses the full trigger threshold, the Escalation Cell convenes an immediate 5-minute verification meeting, confirms the threshold crossing, and issues a formal Trigger Crossing Declaration to the UC within 15 minutes. The UC, upon receiving this declaration, has a standing order to issue the Scenario Beta 500 km evacuation order within 30 minutes without requiring further deliberation or approval.

Responsible Body/Role: Escalation & Scenario Beta Decision Cell (led by USGS Volcano Disaster Assistance Program lead) with immediate notification to UC

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hours 0–72 (T+0 to T+72h), continuous real-time monitoring

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Real-time indicator monitoring and hourly status briefings to UC (scheduled briefings at T+0, T+6, T+12, T+18, T+24, T+30, T+36, T+42, T+48, T+54, T+60, T+66, T+72h)
  • Warning-threshold alerts (80% of trigger threshold) sent to UC and FUCE
  • Trigger Crossing Declaration (if full threshold crossed), signed by USGS lead and issued within 15 minutes of detection
  • UC decision log entry documenting Trigger Crossing Declaration and the Scenario Beta order issued within 30 minutes (if triggered)

Dependencies:

  • Escalation Cell established at T+0
  • Real-time USGS data feeds live and streaming continuously
  • USGS trigger matrix finalized by T+3h
  • UC standing order to issue Scenario Beta order within 30 minutes of Trigger Crossing Declaration

30. UC, upon receiving a Scenario Beta Trigger Crossing Declaration from the Escalation Cell, issues a formal Scenario Beta 500 km Evacuation Order within 30 minutes. The order specifies: (1) the eruption indicators that crossed the trigger threshold; (2) the 500 km radius evacuation boundary; (3) the tiered execution rings (0–100 km organized evacuation, 100–250 km time-banded evacuation, 250–500 km staged departures); (4) the interim Scenario Beta hub destinations (ranked list outside the 500 km ring); (5) the activation of the secondary-stage shelter and logistics plans (pre-authorized buses, rail corridors, secondary hubs with pre-signed host MOUs); (6) instructions to states, National Guard and FEMA to immediately activate all Scenario Beta contingency plans. This order is broadcast via IPAWS, WEA, NOAA Weather Radio, Guard signal bridging and media in English and five languages.

Responsible Body/Role: Unified Command (led by FEMA Region VIII IC, chair)

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), within 30 minutes of Scenario Beta Trigger Crossing Declaration (exact time depends on trigger occurrence)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Formal Scenario Beta 500 km Evacuation Order (signed by FEMA Region VIII IC on behalf of UC)
  • Tiered-execution guidance for the three evacuation rings (0–100 km organized, 100–250 km time-banded, 250–500 km staged)
  • Interim hub-destination list and assignments (which populations to which secondary hubs)
  • Activation orders for secondary-stage shelter, logistics and transport contingencies
  • Broadcast confirmation (IPAWS, WEA, NOAA, Guard signal, media in multiple languages)
  • UC briefing documenting the Scenario Beta escalation and all decisions made in the 30-minute window

Dependencies:

31. Upon issuance of a Scenario Beta 500 km Evacuation Order, the Unified Command immediately convenes an expanded UC Scenario Beta Response Cell, adding representatives from: (1) the secondary hub communities (Denver, Cheyenne, Billings) or their designees; (2) the National Guard regional commanders for out-of-state Guard deployment; (3) the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (if emergency logistics support is needed); (4) representatives from the Department of Transportation (federal coordination of I-15, I-80, I-90 usage and emergency lane closures). This expanded cell meets continuously (at least every 2 hours) to coordinate the execution of the three evacuation rings, the routing of populations to secondary hubs, the activation of bus fleets and rail corridors, and the pre-positioning of supplies at secondary hubs.

Responsible Body/Role: Unified Command (led by FEMA Region VIII IC) expanded with secondary hub representatives, National Guard, USACE and DOT

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), immediately upon Scenario Beta Evacuation Order issuance

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

32. At T+72 hours (end of the 72-hour decision window), the UC holds a formal status briefing documenting: (1) total evacuees received and sheltered (Zone Zero and Zone One); (2) final status of the Scenario Beta escalation (if triggered or if indicators remained below threshold); (3) cumulative supply deliveries (water, N95, fuel) and any shortages or contingency activations; (4) responder casualties or exposure-limit violations; (5) post-event safety assessment for any re-entry or infrastructure restoration activities. The UC transitions governance from 72-hour crisis operations to Months 1–3 (2026-11-14 to 2027-01-14) hardening and post-event review mode, with daily (instead of hourly) briefings and a focus on documentation, MOUs, exercises and after-action planning.

Responsible Body/Role: Unified Command (led by FEMA Region VIII IC, chair)

Suggested Timeframe: Month 0 (2026-10-14), Hour 72 (T+72h)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Scenario Beta status (triggered or not; if triggered, execution summary)

  • Post-event safety assessment and re-entry/infrastructure restoration preliminary guidance
  • UC decision log final entries and closure
  • Transition briefing to Phase 3 (Months 1–3 = 2026-11-14 to 2027-01-14 hardening and post-event review)

FEMA Region VIII IC (UC chair) or designee convenes the first Months 1–3 (2026-11-14 to 2027-01-14) Hardening & Post-Event Review meeting with UC members, specialized advisory-body leads, state emergency managers, USGS, NOAA and NPS representatives. The meeting covers: (1) what went well and what could be improved in the 72-hour response (based on preliminary field observations and responder interviews); (2) a schedule for signed MOUs with the three governors, FEMA Region 10, utilities and Scenario Beta hub communities (target Month 1 = 2026-11-14 completion); (3) a schedule for three after-action reports (one at Month 1 = 2026-11-14 for the 72-hour response, one at Month 2 = 2026-12-14 for MOU and exercise readiness, one at Month 3 = 2027-01-14 for full post-event review); (4) a calendar for three full-scale multi-state exercises (one at Month 2 = 2026-12-14 covering boundary authority transfer and reroutes, one at Month 2.5 = 2026-12-29 covering Scenario Beta evacuation and hub coordination, one at Month 3 = 2027-01-14 covering integrated response) and six smaller operational exercises (shift-rotation, water-convoy, grid-failure recovery, multilingual alert testing, shelter relocation and post-event re-entry).

Responsible Body/Role: FEMA Region VIII IC (UC chair) or designee, with participation from all UC and advisory-body leads

Suggested Timeframe: Month 1 (2026-11-14), Week 1 (first week after T+72h)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

FEMA Region VIII IC (UC chair) and state emergency managers (MT, WY, ID governors or their designees) sign formal Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) confirming: (1) each state's acceptance of the UC's authority to issue Zone One and Scenario Beta evacuation orders; (2) commitment to enforce unified evacuation messaging and shelter assignments on state roads and communities; (3) provision of state resources (highway patrol, National Guard) to support contraflow and perimeter operations; (4) mutual-aid resource sharing (water, fuel, medical supplies) among the three states and FEMA Regions 8 and 10; (5) commitment to participate in post-event exercises and after-action-report development. Simultaneous MOUs are signed with FEMA Region 10 (Seattle), regional utilities (Montana-Dakota Utilities, Pacific Power, Idaho Power) and Scenario Beta secondary hub communities (Denver, Cheyenne, Billings or others outside the 500 km ring). All MOUs are signed by the deadline of Month 1 (2026-11-14).

FEMA Region VIII IC (UC chair) or designee publishes the first After-Action Report (AAR-1: 72-Hour Response) by Month 1 (2026-11-14), documenting: (1) a timeline and narrative of the 72-hour evacuation response (T+0 to T+72h); (2) quantitative outcomes (total evacuees sheltered, supply deliveries, responder incidents, gateway clearance rates); (3) comparison of actual outcomes to pre-planned targets (98% Zone Zero clearance by T+6h, 95% Zone One clearance by T+24h, etc.); (4) critical decisions made and their rationale (recorded from UC decision log); (5) responder feedback and preliminary observations (lessons learned); (6) recommendations for improvements to the governance structure, command protocols, supply logistics or communications. The AAR-1 is distributed to all UC members, state emergency managers, USGS, NOAA, NPS and is published as a public document to maintain transparency.

36. FEMA Region VIII IC (UC chair) or designee convenes the first full-scale multi-state exercise (Exercise-1: 'Cascade Boundary') in Month 2 (2026-12-14), testing the authority-transfer protocols and reroute decision-making across the NPS-to-state boundaries at all three exit gates (West, North, East Entrance). The exercise simulates a Gallatin Canyon blockage at T+3h that requires a 45-minute clearance attempt (proposed threshold) followed by automatic diversion of overflow traffic to the US-89 Gardiner corridor. The exercise tests: (1) whether the Boundary Coordination Officer and state on-scene commanders can issue reroutes within 5 minutes of the blockage detection; (2) whether the COP dashboard is updated in real time with traffic redirects; (3) whether drivers receive updated route guidance via IPAWS, HAR, VMS or printed route cards; (4) whether the diversion adds only the planned 2–4 hours to transit times for affected vehicles, not more. Exercise participants include the FUCE, state traffic-control personnel at each gate, the Authority Cell, the Shelter Siting Panel and a sample of drivers (simulated evacuees in vehicles with communications staff).

Responsible Body/Role: FEMA Region VIII IC (UC chair) or designee, with FUCE Operations Chief as exercise director

Suggested Timeframe: Month 2 (2026-12-14), Week 1 (2026-12-14, within first week of month)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Exercise-1 planning memo and scenario description
  • Exercise-1 'Cascade Boundary' simulation (2-4 hours duration, in-person or hybrid)
  • Post-exercise hot wash (immediate feedback from participants on what worked and what didn't)
  • Exercise-1 After-Action Report (preliminary, by Month 2 = 2026-12-14 Week 2)

Dependencies:

  • AAR-1 (72-Hour Response) published by Month 1 (2026-11-14)
  • All three states and FUCE committed to exercise participation

FEMA Region VIII IC (UC chair) or designee convenes the second full-scale multi-state exercise (Exercise-2: 'Ring Dispersal') in Month 2.5 (2026-12-29), testing Scenario Beta execution: the Escalation Cell simulates a USGS Trigger Crossing Declaration at a notional T+36h, triggering the UC to issue a 500 km Evacuation Order. The exercise tests: (1) whether the UC issues the order within 30 minutes of trigger declaration; (2) whether the expanded Scenario Beta Response Cell activates and coordinates ring-by-ring evacuation (0–100 km organized, 100–250 km time-banded, 250–500 km staged); (3) whether secondary hub communities (Denver, Cheyenne) receive and begin processing evacuees within their assigned rings; (4) whether bus fleets and rail corridors are deployed to move evacuees from primary shelters (Bozeman, Idaho Falls) to secondary hubs within the planned timelines; (5) whether supply pre-positioning at secondary hubs is confirmed and adequate. Exercise participants include the UC, FUCE, secondary hub emergency managers, National Guard, bus and rail operators, and simulated evacuee populations.

Responsible Body/Role: FEMA Region VIII IC (UC chair) or designee, with FUCE Operations Chief as exercise director

Suggested Timeframe: Month 2.5 (2026-12-29, between Months 2 and 3 = 2026-12-14, 2027-01-14)

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Exercise-2 'Ring Dispersal' simulation (4-6 hours duration, multi-state, in-person or hybrid)

FEMA Region VIII IC (UC chair) or designee convenes the third full-scale multi-state exercise (Exercise-3: 'Yellowstone Integrated Response') in Month 3 (2027-01-14), integrating all elements of the response: the Escalation Cell simulates real-time eruption indicators during a 12-hour compressed exercise timeline, the Unified Command makes strategic decisions (zone expansion, Scenario Beta triggers), the FUCE executes tactical operations (contraflow, tow dispatch, water convoy routing), the Responder Health Board manages shift rotation and fatigue, the Authority Cell coordinates boundary transfers, the Shelter Siting Panel monitors PM10 and triggers relocations, and the Scenario Beta Response Cell (if triggered) activates ring-by-ring evacuation. The exercise tests the integrated governance structure under conditions approaching the actual 72-hour response complexity. Exercise participants include all UC and advisory-body members, state emergency managers, FUCE staff, utilities, hospitals, shelter operators, bus and rail carriers, and secondary hub representatives.

Responsible Body/Role: FEMA Region VIII IC (UC chair) or designee, with FUCE Operations Chief as exercise director

Key Outputs/Deliverables:

  • Exercise-3 'Yellowstone Integrated Response' simulation (8-12 hours duration, 12-hour compressed timeline, multi-state, in-person at FEMA RRCC and FUCE forward element)

  • Exercise-3 After-Action Report (detailed, by Month 3 = 2027-01-14 Week 3 or 4)

Dependencies:

  • AAR-1 (72-Hour Response) and Exercise-1/2 reports completed and reviewed by Month 2 (2026-12-14)
  • Signed MOUs with all states, Region 10, utilities and secondary hubs by Month 1 (2026-11-14) end

39. FEMA Region VIII IC (UC chair) or designee publishes the final comprehensive After-Action Report (AAR-3: 72-Hour Response + Months 1–3 = 2026-11-14 to 2027-01-14 Hardening & Exercises) by the end of Month 3 (2027-01-14), consolidating lessons learned from: (1) the actual 72-hour response (T+0 to T+72h); (2) the Months 1–3 (2026-11-14 to 2027-01-14) MOU negotiations and governance formalization; (3) the three full-scale exercises (Exercise-1 Boundary, Exercise-2 Scenario Beta, Exercise-3 Integrated Response) and six smaller operational exercises. The report documents: (1) what the governance structure achieved during the 72-hour crisis (strengths and weaknesses); (2) what improvements have been made to governance, command protocols, communications, supply logistics and authority clarification during Months 1–3 (2026-11-14 to 2027-01-14); (3) what gaps or risks remain and recommendations for future planning cycles; (4) updated governance best practices and lessons learned to inform planning for future Yellowstone eruption events or similar multi-state volcanic evacuations. AAR-3 is published as an official FEMA and NPS document and distributed to all stakeholders and to the National Incident Management System (NIMS) community for use in national emergency management planning.

Decision Escalation Matrix
